blocks.text: Batch jobs answer "what happened yesterday?". Many products need "what's happening now": fraud scoring within a second of a transaction, live dashboards, trending topics, surge pricing, alerting. Stream processors (Flink, Kafka Streams, Spark Structured Streaming, Beam/Dataflow) run continuous queries over unbounded event streams, keeping state and producing results incrementally.

Events arrive late and out of order: a phone loses signal and uploads ten minutes of events at once. If you bucket by **processing time** (when the event reached you), those events land in the wrong minute. Bucket by **event time** (the timestamp in the event) — then you need a rule for when a window is complete. That's the **watermark**: a moving estimate of "we've now seen all events up to time T".

head: Window
Shape
Example
rows: Fixed length, overlapping (last 5 min, every 1 min)
Gap-based: closes after N minutes of inactivity

blocks.caption: A late event and the watermark

items.title: Keyed state
items.text: Each operator instance holds state for its key range (counts, join buffers) in local RocksDB — fast, no network calls.

items.title: Checkpoint
items.text: Periodically (e.g. every 10 s), barriers flow through the graph and every operator snapshots its state to durable storage, aligned with the source offsets.

items.title: Failure
items.text: Restart from the last checkpoint: restore state and rewind Kafka offsets to the checkpointed positions.

items.title: Output
items.text: Make the sink transactional (two-phase commit tied to checkpoints) or idempotent (upsert by deterministic key) so replays don't double-write.

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: "Exactly-once" in streaming means exactly-once *effect on state and output*, not that each event is physically processed once. Replays happen; idempotent or transactional sinks hide them.

steps.label: WAL change via logical replication slot
search indexer, cache invalidator, warehouse loader

blocks.caption: CDC from Postgres to everything else

items: No dual writes: the database's own log is the source, so every committed change is captured exactly in commit order.
Consumers can be added later and backfilled from a snapshot + the log.
Watch replication-slot lag: a stalled consumer makes Postgres retain WAL and fill the disk.
**Stream–table join:** enrich each click with ad metadata held as a changelog-backed table in state (or a cached lookup).
**Stream–stream join:** match impressions with clicks within a time window; both sides buffered in state for the window.
Repartition (shuffle) by the join key first so matching events meet on the same instance.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Events land in Kafka keyed by ad id; Flink aggregates them in one-minute event-time windows with a short allowed lateness, checkpoints state every few seconds, and upserts results by (ad id, minute) into the OLAP store, so a replay can't double count. Database changes reach search and the warehouse through Debezium CDC.
